interest: This document illustrates the State Department's tracking and cross-referencing of intelligence regarding potential Japanese espionage, subversive activities, and diplomatic presence in peripheral neutral colonial territories during the wartime/interwar era. Even when reports indicated a negative finding—confirming the absence of Japanese representation or interests in Portuguese East Africa (Mozambique)—such inquiries were systematically catalogued under specialized military and subversive activity decimal classifications.
overview: This file consists of a single 'List of Papers' docket sheet for State Department decimal file 894.20253N, titled 'Alleged Japanese subversive activities in Portuguese East Africa.' Classified as a non-jacket case, it records a single entry (Sub No. 1) referencing telegram No. 47 sent from Lourenço Marques by Preston on March 19. The purport notes that the telegram reported on Japanese representation and interests in Portuguese East Africa, informing that there were none, and directs researchers to the primary filing location under 853n.00/50.

subfiles.summary: This docket sheet records paper number 1 under decimal file 894.20253N regarding alleged Japanese subversive activities in Portuguese East Africa. It lists Telegram No. 47 sent at 6 p.m. on March 19 from Preston in Lourenço Marques concerning Japanese representation and interests. The purport indicates that there were no Japanese interests or representations found, cross-referencing the full document to decimal file 853n.00/50.
